bullet_points: Revenue for the fourth quarter was a record \$39.3 billion,up 78% from a year ago and up 12% sequentially. Fiscal year revenue was \$130.5 billion, up 114% from a year ago.

Data Center revenue for fiscal 2025 was \$115.2 billion,up 142% from a year ago. Data Center revenue for the fourth quarter was a record,up 93% from a year ago and up 16% sequentially. The strong year-on-year and sequential growth was driven by demand for our accelerated computing platform used for large language models, recommendation engines,and generative Al applications. We delivered \$11.O bilion of Blackwellarchitecture revenue in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025,the fastest product ramp in our company's history. Blackwell sales were led by large cloud service providers which represented approximately 5O% of our Data Center revenue.Data Center compute revenue was \$32.6 bilion,up 116% from a year ago and up 18% sequentially,driven by demand for our Blackwell computing_platform_and sequential growth from our H2Oo offering. Networking revenue was \$3.0 bilion,down 9% from a year ago and down 3% sequentially. We are transitioning from small NVLink 8 with Infiniband to large NVLink 72 with Spectrum X. Networking experienced growth in Ethernet for Al, which includes Spectrum-X end-to-end ethernet platform,and NVLink products related to the ramp of our Grace Blackwell platform.

Gaming revenue for fiscal 2O25 was up 9% from a year ago,driven by sales of our GeForce RTX 40 Series GPUs. Gaming revenue for the fourth quarter was down 11% from a year ago and down 22% sequentially, due to limited supply for both Blackwell and Ada GPUs.

Professional Visualization revenue for fiscal 2O25 was up 21% from a year ago. Professional Visualization revenue for the fourth quarter was up lO% from a year ago and up 5% sequentially. These increases were driven by the continued ramp of Ada RTX GPU workstations for use cases such as generative Al-powered design,simulation,and engineering.

Automotive revenue for fiscal 2O25 was up 55% from a year ago. Automotive revenue for the fourth quarter was up 103% from a year ago and up 27% sequentially. These increases were driven by sales of our self-driving platforms.
Fiscal 2025 GAAP and Non-GAAP gross margin increased from a year ago,driven by a higher mix of Data Center revenue.

GAAP operating expenses for the fourth quarter were up 48% from a year ago and up 9% sequentially，and non-GAAP operating expenses were up 53% from a year ago and up 11% sequentially. Fiscal 2025 GAAP and non-GAAP operating expenses were up 45% and 50% from a year ago,respectively.The fourth quarter and fiscal 2O25 year-on-year increases were primarily driven by higher compensation and benefits expenses due to employee growth and compensation increases, and engineering development,compute and infrastructure costs for new product introductions.The sequential increases were primarily driven by engineering development, compute and infrastructure costs for new product introductions.

Interest income for the fourth quarter and fiscal year was \$511 millon and \$1.8 billon,respectively, up from a year ago and sequentialy,reflecting growth in cash,cash equivalents,and marketable securities.Net gains from non-marketable and publicly-held equity securities for the fourth quarter were \$727 million, reflecting fair value adjustments and sales of equity investments.

Cash,cash equivalents and marketable securities were \$43.2 billion,up from \$26.0 billion a year ago and \$38.5 billon a quarter ago.The increases primarily reflect higher revenue partially offset by stock repurchases.
Accounts receivable was \$23.1 billion with 53 days sales outstanding (DSO).

Inventory was \$10.1 billon with 86 days sales of inventory (DSl). Inventory increased from \$7.7 billion, and DSl increased from 78 days sequentially. Purchase commitments and obligations for inventory and manufacturing capacity were \$30.8 bilion， including new capacity commitments and components. Supply and capacity prepayments were \$5.1 billion.

Other non-inventory purchase obligations were \$14.3 bilion, including \$10.9 billion of multi-year cloud service agreements. We expect cloud service agreements to be used to support our research and development efforts and our DGX Cloud offerings.

Cash flow from operating activities was \$16.6 bilion,up from \$11.5 billon a year ago and down from \$17.6 bllion a quarter ago.Fiscal year cash flow from operating activities was \$64.1 billion,up from \$28.1 bilion a year ago.The year-on-year increases reflect higher revenue.The sequential decrease was driven by a higher accounts receivable balance due to shipment linearity and increased inventory to support our Blackwell product ramp.

We utilized cash of \$8.1 billion towards shareholder returns, including \$7.8 billon in share repurchases and \$245 milion in cash dividends.In fiscal 2O25，we utilized cash of \$34.5 billion towards shareholder returns,including \$33.7 billion in share repurchases and \$834 million in cash dividends.
Revenue is expected to be \$43.0 billion, plus or minus 2%.
GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are expected to be 70.6% and 71.0%, respectively, plus or minus 50 basis points.
GAAP and non-GAAP operating expenses are expected to be approximately \$5.2 bilion and \$3.6 billion, respectively.

Outlook for the first quarter of fiscal 2026 is as follows:

Revenue is expected to be \$43.0 billion, plus or minus 2%.   
GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are expected to be 70.6% and 71.0%, respectively, plus or minus 50 basis points.   
GAAP and non-GAAP operating expenses are expected to be approximately \$5.2 bilion and \$3.6 billion, respectively.   
GAAP and non-GAAP other income and expense are expected to be an income of approximately \$4Oo milion,excluding gains and losses from non-marketable and publicly-held equity securities.   
GAAP and non-GAAP tax rates are expected to be 17.0%, plus or minus 1%,excluding any discrete items.
